newsitem.title: FIJI: Striking Fiji sugar unionists ordered back to work.
newsitem.headline: Striking Fiji sugar unionists ordered back to work.

text.p: Fiji's Sugar Tribunal said on Friday it had ordered striking members of the Fiji Sugar and General Workers Union to return to work on Saturday.
However, union general secretary, Felix Anthony, said he would meet with members on Saturday to discuss the ruling and would seek legal advice next Tuesday.
"The parties are bound by law to return to work unless they want to challenge this order in a court of law," Sugar Tribunal acting chief, Cyril Don Aidney said.
Aidney said there were measures the tribunal could take if the union defied the order.
He also said that Fiji's sugar exports had already been affected by the strike, adding that Fiji Sugar Corp (FSC) had been unable to make some export commitments.
The return to work order on Friday marked the fifth strike day for 2,000 union members.
Aidney said he had ordered a joint FSC and union committee examination of any submission by the union on health and safety matters at FSC work places.
This has been ruled as the substance of the strike.
The parties have been called to appear before the Tribunal again next Wednesday.
Before the strike, FSC had forecast Fiji's 1997 raw sugar production at 440,000 tonnes, down from 475,000 tonnes in 1996.
The 1997 crush had been running well before the strike, FSC recently said.
